subject: Capacity SKU exchange, burst triggers, and proposed SLA credit mechanics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mednexa.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@mednexa.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Capacity SKU exchange, burst triggers, and proposed SLA credit mechanics

Oliver / Contracts team —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our discussion, I attached a short definition sheet (RDW_Dedicated_Sku_Definitions_v2.pdf) that maps the capacity (vRAM-hours / reserved GPU buckets) to the throughput guarantees we propose for MedNexa's commitment. The three items we'd like you to confirm so the next contract iteration can be precise: 

1) Terminology: we define a "Capacity Unit" as 1 reserved GPU * 720 hours/month at the agreed SKU performance profile (e.g., A100x2-equivalent). Does that align to your procurement team's expectation?
2) Burst policy: we allow short bursts up to 40% above baseline sustained throughput for up to 2 hours/day; bursts beyond this will consume the customer's burst buffer (pre-purchased or billed at on-demand rates). Please confirm acceptable threshold or propose alternatives.
3) SLA credit triggers: we proposed a 3-tier ladder tied to sustained p50/p95 latency and availability for the dedicated pool. See the attached SLA_Credit_Table.csv. For redlines, we are flexible on the remedy ladder but need clear definitions for "throughput impact" versus transient packet loss.

Next steps: if Contracts can send back a redline with terms for amortization and discounting by 2027-08-06 we can move to an internal approvals pass.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: RDW_Dedicated_Sku_Definitions_v2.pdf

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@mednexa.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mednexa.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@mednexa.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Capacity SKU exchange, burst triggers, and proposed SLA credit mechanics

Thanks Ben — Priya (procurement) here. Quick clarifications before legal starts heavy redlines: 

- The "Capacity Unit" definition is OK but can you confirm the underlying GPU equivalence matrix for quantized models? We run a mix of LLMs (1.3B - 34B) and need per-model equivalence for cost allocation.
- Burst: 40% / 2 hours/day is reasonable but procurement would prefer a soft cap where the first 4 hours/month are included, then billed. Can you support a small monthly burst buffer?
- SLA credits: we need clarity on how credits apply when capacity is reserved but traffic is routed to fallback hosted instances (if private pool degraded). That scenario came up in our internal ops review.

Can you have engineering put a short note on the equivalence table and confirm burst buffer options? If you can, we'll ask legal to turn around redlines by Monday.

Best,
Priya Shah
Senior Procurement Manager, MedNexa
priya.shah@mednexa.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@mednexa.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Capacity SKU exchange, burst triggers, and proposed SLA credit mechanics

Priya — looping in Dev to call out the equivalence and fallback behavior. Short answers: 

- Equivalence matrix: attached page 2 of RDW_Dedicated_Sku_Definitions_v2 has per-model throughput multipliers (we'll export them into a CSV). For quantized runs we show a ~1.6x effective vRAM improvement for int8 variants; I'll have Dev add an explicit per-model column.
- Burst buffer: we can offer a small monthly buffer (we proposed 5% of committed CU hours as a prepaid burst buffer) — but we can flex to a fixed 4 hours/month if that makes procurement happier.
- Fallback routing: by default, we don't move traffic off the dedicated pool unless the policy explicitly triggers (capacity exhaustion or emergency failover). If fallback to hosted occurs, it is considered a "service degradation" for SLAs; credits apply to the dedicated commit per the ladder. We can add language that differentiates deliberate emergency failover (customer-approved) vs. automatic fallback.

Ben — I'm attaching Draft_Redlines_MedNexa_20270803.docx with suggested contract language for definitions and the remediation ladder. Priya / Oliver — tell us which burst buffer approach you prefer and we'll produce a clean mark.

Lauren
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0248

Attachments: Draft_Redlines_MedNexa_20270803.docx

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@mednexa.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Aug 2027 07:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Capacity SKU exchange, burst triggers, and proposed SLA credit mechanics

Priya / team —

Quick technical note to include exactly what Lauren called out: 

1) GPU equivalence: we benchmarked on A100-40GB x1 and an internal vRAM-equivalence number is used to map model families. Example excerpt: 7B FP16 @ 1-token/seq -> baseline throughput X. Quantized int8 shows ~1.55x throughput per vRAM for our runtime for that family; for larger 34B models the benefit is smaller (~1.25x). I'll paste an export into the contract appendix.

2) Burst buffer implementation: operationally we keep a separate meter for bursts. If you choose the prepaid buffer (e.g., 4 hours/month at the committed bucket size), we will deduct from buffer first then bill on-demand for additional minutes.

3) Fallback semantics: automatic fallback occurs only when the dedicated pool reports >95% queue saturation for 3 consecutive minutes OR a regional outage is declared. Those are the objective triggers we recommend. If fallback is customer-initiated (ops runbook), we flag that as customer-requested and do not count it as a remedial SLA event.

Happy to provide the raw benchmark CSV.

— Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

From: Contracts Team <contracts@mednexa.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mednexa.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@mednexa.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 14:10:00 +0000
Subject: MedNexa - redlined Dedicated Capacity terms (first pass)

Hi Lauren / Ben —

Attached are the first-pass redlines from MedNexa Legal. High level: 

- We accepted the Capacity Unit definition but requested an explicit appendix with per-model equivalence numbers and the quantized multipliers (good to see you'll add those).
- We replaced the 2-hour/day burst language with: "Customers receive a prepaid monthly burst allowance equal to 4 hours at committed bucket throughput; additional burst consumption billed at on-demand rates."
- We added language that automatic fallback to hosted will only count as an SLA event if our traffic was routed offsite without written notification and remediation attempts. (We request a 15-minute canned notification window before automated fallback).

We included a handful of redlines to the credit ladder: we prefer a monetary credit over service-day credits in specific tiers; see the attached Draft_Redlines_MedNexa_20270803.docx with tracked changes.

Please respond with your comments by EOD Wednesday so we can align procurement / CFO sign-off.

Thanks,
MedNexa Contracts (on behalf of Oliver Grant)
contracts@mednexa.com

Attachments: Draft_Redlines_MedNexa_20270803.docx, SLA_Credit_Table.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Contracts Team <contracts@mednexa.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@mednexa.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MedNexa - redlined Dedicated Capacity terms (first pass)

Team —

Appreciate the quick review and the clear asks. Short responses and path forward: 

• Capacity appendix: Dev will export the benchmark CSV and we'll append it to the agreement as a non-normative appendix.
• Burst buffer: happy to commit to the prepaid 4 hours/month model with roll-over of unused minutes up to two months (to help handle piloting spikes).
• Automatic fallback notification: we can configure a 10-minute notification window (we can agree to 10 instead of 15) and provide an ops webhook for your SREs so you receive the event stream.
• Credits vs. monetary: we usually do monetary credits applied to committed spend; we'll propose a hybrid ladder that caps credits at a % of monthly committed spend per month (see revised SLA_Credit_Table.csv attached).

I'll route this to my manager for the final pricing concessions approval — if procurement is comfortable we can lock pricing and submit for signatures by Friday.

Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: SLA_Credit_Table.csv
